title: Regional hot-spare buffer simulation and recommended rotation policy
content:
Purpose:
This note captures the Monte Carlo simulation we ran to evaluate region-level hot-spare sizing and a lightweight rotational policy for multi-region GPU fleet continuity. Goal: keep customer-visible capacity shortfall below 1% of requests over rolling 30-day windows while minimizing idle cost.

Executive summary:
- Simulation: 10,000 trials of 30-day windows using observed hourly traffic and failure distributions.
- Recommendation: Maintain a hot-spare buffer equal to 7% of production capacity in each primary region for steady-state; additionally, maintain a global rotational pool sized at 2% of total fleet to rebalance across regions after prolonged outages (>24h).
- Rotation cadence: rotate hot-spare assignment weekly (Friday 02:00 UTC) to avoid cold-starts and evenly distribute wear.
- Expected outcomes: reduces multi-region outage impact on capacity shortfalls from median 3.1% to 0.7% at 99th percentile, with an estimated incremental cost of ~3.2% of fleet monthly OPEX.

Base assumptions (inputs used in sim):
- Fleet: 2100 prod GPUs distributed across 4 primary regions (NA-1: 900, EU-1: 600, APAC-1: 400, NA-2: 200).
- Traffic: hourly token demand trace sampled from April 2026 production telemetry (workload mix: 62% generation, 28% chat, 10% rerank).
- Failure model: per-cluster outage probability modeled as Poisson with lambda=0.015/day for transient incidents and lambda=0.002/day for multi-hour regional incidents.
- Recovery: automated failover + capacity warm-up takes 6-12 minutes for prefixcache-safe workloads; full warm-up for cold replicas (quantized models) assumed 45 minutes.
- SLO: maintain token-serving capacity so that queued requests do not exceed 0.5% p99 latency degradation target.

Simulation design:
- Monte Carlo: 10k runs, 30-day windows. Each run samples outages, traffic spikes, and stateful cache hit rates.
- Scenarios: single-region partial outage, full-region outage, concurrent dual-region stress, and sustained traffic surge (x1.6 sustained for 6 hours).
- Policies compared: (A) no regional hot-spare (current baseline), (B) regional hot-spare buffer only, (C) regional buffer + global rotational pool.

Key results (summary):
- Baseline (A): 99th-percentile capacity shortfall = 3.1% of served tokens; tail incidents required emergency burst allocations in 22% of runs.
- Policy B (7% region buffer): 99th-percentile shortfall = 1.4%; emergency bursts in 9% of runs.
- Policy C (7% region buffer + 2% global rotation): 99th-percentile shortfall = 0.7%; emergency bursts in 2.8% of runs.
- Cost delta: Policy C increases reserved idle GPU-hours by ~3.2% relative to baseline; estimated monthly cost uplift = $64k (based on current committed pricing).

Operational recommendations:
- Hot-spare sizing: provision dedicated hot-spare instances equal to 7% of the region's effective serving capacity. For small regions (<250 GPUs), round up to minimum 20 GPUs to avoid fragmentation.
- Rotational pool: create a global pool (2% of fleet) of pre-provisioned nodes that are NOT pinned to a region and can be reprovisioned within 20 minutes to the target region when capacity imbalance triggers.
- Triggering rules: start rotation when projected regional deficit >4% over next 2 hours OR single-region outage >30 minutes. Implement graceful draining for rotated nodes to preserve KV-cache where possible.
- Canary and rollout: stage policy C in one NA region for 4 weeks; observe p99 latency and cost, then expand to EU followed by APAC.

Failover sequencing (detailed):
1) Local autoscale and preemption avoidance (immediate).
2) Regional hot-spare activation (0-2 minutes): switch traffic to hot-spare zone within same region.
3) Short rotation from global pool (20-40 minutes): reprovision and attach global nodes to affected region.
4) Cross-region routing fallback (40+ minutes): route lower-priority traffic to secondary region model variants (quantized) with degradation notice.

Cost vs reliability tradeoffs:
- Baseline to Policy C: +3.2% OPEX for ~>2.4x reduction in emergency bursts.
- Sensitivity: if region outage rate doubles, required hot-spare buffer grows to ~10% to keep 99th-tail <1%.

Action items (owners and dates):
- Diego Morales: build rotational pool provisioning automation (infra-as-code templates) — due 2026-06-16.
- Rina Khatri: update routing policy library to support dynamic hot-spare activation flags — due 2026-06-09.
- Ben Cho: instrument new telemetry tags for hot-spare activation and rotation events — due 2026-06-04.
- Aisha Patel (owner): run staged rollout in NA-1 and generate post-mortem after 4 weeks — due 2026-07-14.

Open questions / risks:
- Cache cold-start impact on high-recall workloads is still under-modeled; need real-world smoke tests with quantized model variants.
- Regulatory constraint: APAC data residency may limit rotational pool reassignments across regions. Legal to review (linked artifact: JIRA:LEGAL-112).
- Cost model sensitivity to spot pricing volatility (we assumed committed prices) — finance to validate.

Appendix: simulation params (for infra-sim team)
- Script: infra-simulations/sim_hotspare.py commit 9f7a2b (GITHUB: repo/infra-simulations/pull/87)
- Trials: 10_000; window_days: 30; seed: 20260503
- Failure dist: poisson(lambda_transient=0.015, lambda_multihr=0.002)
- Traffic scale factors: sample distribution from 2026-04 telemetry multiplied by 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 for surge scenarios.
- Output metrics: percent of served tokens with queued latency > target, number of emergency bursts, cumulative idle GPU-hours, regional shortfall percentiles.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working doc; please comment inline. Priority feedback: is 7% per-region buffer acceptable given procurement constraints? Are there objections to weekly rotation cadence? Any missing failure modes to model?
